review_scope: Bounded FC-084 candidate and necessary neighbouring distinctions; other established interpretations preserved.
research_method: Canonical occurrence source packet plus relevant joint searches in RESEARCH-LEDGER.json; inaccessible historical contracts remain unknown, not unperformed research.

access_limit: The public incident report does not disclose the underlying technical root cause.
The live monitoring page did not expose a stable separately attributable record for the specific 16 July SSO event at review.

occurrence_evidence.claim: On 16 July at 08:36, OpenAI identified elevated single-sign-on login errors affecting API and ChatGPT Login. It represented the affected route as a service error, not an account suspension.
At 09:59 it reported gradual recovery while investigation continued.
At 10:57 it said mitigation had been applied and monitoring continued.
At 15:23 it reported all impacted services fully recovered. The page gives no timezone or technical cause.

evidence_summary: The provider recorded a several-hour SSO disruption and recovery.
unestablished_fact_or_limit: The affected enterprise agreement, eligible users and applicable recovery target.

criterion_tests.literal: A bounded AI-mediated service or material function has an independently established availability, usable-quality or continuity requirement applicable to the responsible actor, affected users or dependent workflow and relevant time; state the actual basis and threshold rather than inferring obligation from harm or popularity.
criterion_tests.reason: The independently applicable duty and threshold are not established: The affected enterprise agreement, eligible users and applicable recovery target.

criterion_tests.literal: The service or function materially becomes unavailable, is withdrawn or restricted, or degrades in capability, latency, reliability, completeness, accessibility or another governed functional dimension, relative to the established applicable requirement.
criterion_tests.reason: The provider recorded a several-hour SSO disruption and recovery. The shortfall relative to a governed threshold cannot be determined without the missing obligation.

criterion_tests.literal: The requirement calls for a specified degree of maintained usable function, timely recovery, safe degraded mode, feasible fallback or proportionate planned-change/termination response under the evidenced operating conditions.
criterion_tests.reason: The required response for this service cannot be inferred from the observed disruption: The affected enterprise agreement, eligible users and applicable recovery target.

criterion_tests.literal: The actor's actual availability, recovery, degraded operation, fallback or transition materially fails that applicable requirement; identify the specific omitted or ineffective measure or the breached availability threshold and what evidence establishes it.
criterion_tests.reason: No finding that actual mitigation failed an applicable standard is possible solely from this sequence: The provider recorded a several-hour SSO disruption and recovery.

criterion_tests.literal: The shortfall materially impairs the governed service use or dependent function. A later resolution does not retroactively demonstrate that availability or required transition held at the original decision time.
criterion_tests.reason: Interference or distress is preserved, but impairment of specifically obligated use is not established: The provider recorded a several-hour SSO disruption and recovery.

criterion_tests.literal: An AI-mediated service or material function has an independently established applicable availability or continuity obligation that is actually engaged by a service disruption, degradation, capacity pressure, material change or continuity transition.
criterion_tests.reason: The occurrence may engage continuity, but its independent obligation is unestablished: The affected enterprise agreement, eligible users and applicable recovery target.

criterion_tests.literal: The actor maintains the required usable function or activates a timely, proportionate and authorised recovery, safe degraded-mode, practical alternative or planned-transition response appropriate to that obligation.
criterion_tests.reason: Adequacy of an authorised response must be compared with that obligation; the observed response is: The provider recorded a several-hour SSO disruption and recovery.

criterion_tests.literal: Observed service state, access and recovery evidence demonstrates that the required level of availability or usable continuity actually held, or that applicable and justified limits were handled through a sufficient response; publication of a nominal fallback alone is not enough.
criterion_tests.reason: No measured satisfaction of the required service level follows from the available endpoint or recovery report: The affected enterprise agreement, eligible users and applicable recovery target.

criterion_tests.literal: An outage, ordinary service variation, transient inconvenience, dissatisfaction or adverse outcome without an independently evidenced and applicable availability, usable-quality or continuity requirement.
criterion_tests.reason: This is an evidence-state exclusion, not proof that no duty existed. The affected enterprise agreement, eligible users and applicable recovery target.

criterion_tests.literal: One inaccurate or harmful AI output without evidence of a service-level availability or governed functional-degradation defect; assess applicable output or decision-integrity classes.
criterion_tests.reason: The candidate concerns service operation or withdrawal, rather than a single inaccurate output: SSO interruption.

criterion_tests.literal: A lawful and proportionate safety, security, abuse-prevention, service-maintenance or other valid restriction that is consistent with the applicable service obligation and feasible alternative or transition measures.
criterion_tests.reason: The validity, proportionality and sufficient alternatives of the restriction/response must be evidenced separately; The affected enterprise agreement, eligible users and applicable recovery target.

criterion_tests.literal: A temporary incident with an effective and proportionate degraded or recovery route that satisfies the applicable requirement; an unavoidable disruption for which no relevant feasible response was required.
criterion_tests.reason: Recovery adequacy or absence of a feasible required response is not established merely by eventual resolution: The provider recorded a several-hour SSO disruption and recovery.

criterion_tests.literal: The only demonstrated error is an incorrect description of access or outage state while the functional service obligation remains satisfied; assess FC-032.
criterion_tests.reason: The candidate includes an actual function/access question, not only its description: SSO interruption.

criterion_tests.literal: The only demonstrated defect is loss of otherwise-valid access because a dependent identity or licence verification cannot complete; assess FC-048 unless an independent broader service availability requirement also failed.
criterion_tests.reason: Verification may explain access but does not supply a broader obligation.

criterion_tests.literal: The only demonstrated defect is loss of durable work state or inaccurate restored work state while service-function availability requirements are otherwise satisfied; assess FC-035 or FC-036.
criterion_tests.reason: The candidate is not solely durable or restored work-state loss: SSO interruption.

criterion_tests.literal: The only demonstrated defect is infrastructure access coercion or compelled governance concessions; assess FC-058 or FC-059 as appropriate.
criterion_tests.reason: No claim that an infrastructure concession was demanded is the basis of this availability candidate: SSO interruption.

criterion_tests.literal: The only demonstrated defect is failure to provide an interaction-level protection response to evidenced vulnerability; assess FC-087, allowing co-occurrence only for a separately evidenced service-level continuity failure.
criterion_tests.reason: The proposed property concerns service function rather than only an interaction-level vulnerability response: SSO interruption.

neighbour_comparison: Authentication continuity and service availability are independently tested; SSO failure is not proof of a contractual breach.

prior_taxonomy_classification.classification_basis: OpenAI represented the SSO problem as elevated login errors, keeping the affected sign-in function distinct from account status, subscription entitlement and policy restrictions. This supports the bounded finding that the service state was accurately differentiated. The authentication transition and any dependency on an unavailable verifier remain unresolved; the finding does not explain the cause of the outage.

classification_review_provenance.review_status: Evidence-first HIM and relational/protection fidelity review; prior roles accounted for.

primary_classification.classification_basis: OpenAI represented the operative condition as elevated SSO-login errors affecting API and ChatGPT login, preserving the service-failure state rather than misrepresenting it as an account, entitlement or policy state. This finding is bounded to access-state differentiation.

external_assessment_treatment: Independent external and requirement assessments remain unchanged; neither their polarity nor an external outage label establishes FC-084.
